source: Mathias (2014) Exploration, exploitation, ambidexterity and firm performance: a meta-analysis (OpenAlex abstract)
finding: Meta-analysis finds strong performance effects for exploration and exploitation alone. Ambidexterity gives a WEAKER effect than a focus on either one. This is against received theory.
numbers: 117 studies, more than 21,000 firms. No effect sizes in the abstract.
quote: ambidexterity yields weaker effects than a focus on either exploration or exploitation
limits: Abstract only. Coding differs from Junni 2013.
agent_relevance: Balance is not free. A fixed 50/50 split of tokens between explore and exploit may lose to a focused arm.

source: He and Wong (2004) Organization Science abstract (Crossref)
finding: 206 manufacturing firms. Interaction of explorative and exploitative innovation strategies relates positively to sales growth. Relative imbalance relates negatively to sales growth.
numbers: N=206 firms; outcome sales growth rate. Citations: Crossref 2934, OpenAlex 4489, IDEAS 777.
limits: Abstract only; coefficients not read. a11 count of 777 is an IDEAS-only count.
agent_relevance: Supports balance plus interaction, but only for sales growth in manufacturing.

source: Cao, Gedajlovic and Zhang (2009) Organization Science abstract (Crossref)
finding: Splits ambidexterity into a balance dimension (BD) and a combined-magnitude dimension (CD). Both help; high BD plus high CD adds synergy. BD helps resource-constrained firms more; CD helps resource-rich firms more.
numbers: No sample numbers in the abstract.
agent_relevance: At small token budgets balance may matter more; at large budgets doing both at high levels. Testable at equal tokens.

source: Clauss et al. (2020) Organizational ambidexterity and competitive advantage: strategic agility (OpenAlex abstract)
finding: In 150 German mid-sized engineering firms an ambidextrous strategy seemed to hurt competitive advantage. Exploration alone, or exploitation plus strategic agility, helped.
quote: an ambidextrous strategy seems to even negatively influence the competitive advantage of a firm
limits: Abstract only; outcome is competitive advantage, not sales growth.
agent_relevance: A second negative result against balance.

source: Jansen et al. (2006) Management Science abstract (Crossref), recheck of a13-a16
finding: Abstract agrees in direction with the betas in a14 and a15: centralisation hurts exploratory, formalisation helps exploitative, connectedness helps both, dynamism favours exploration, competitiveness favours exploitation for financial performance.
agent_relevance: Environment decides which side to favour.

source: Krishnamurthy et al. (2024) abstract (OpenAlex) and Binz and Schulz (PNAS) abstract (Crossref), recheck of b17 and c12
finding: Only one GPT-4 configuration (chain of thought plus externally summarised history) explored well; the rest did not. Binz and Schulz: GPT-3 beats humans in a bandit task yet shows no signature of directed exploration.
numbers: Qualitative in abstracts. The over-60% suffix failure figure in b17 was not rechecked.
agent_relevance: Exploration should be forced by the scaffold, not left to the model.
